ctx.x: You can’t see this but I’m looking at the wall in front of me and I have a printout of the top 100 Charlie Calello hits and arrangements. And I’ve zoomed in on a couple. And I want to sort of dissect the “Lover’s Concerto” if you don’t mind. Because as you said, this hit a nerve with me. And I noticed that, I really got into the deep end with this because I was timing, how long was the melody. And you know the first phrase is like 16 seconds, and then there’s two of them. A 16 second intro and then the whole…

No. In fact when I made that record – I’ll back up a couple of beats – Sandy Linzer wrote the song with Denny Randell. Sandy Linzer also wrote “Dawn (Go Away)” with Bob Gaudio, and he became one of the writers of the Four Seasons. My father actually introduced me to him. So after they had a couple of hit records with Bob Crewe they © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

decided to produce a record on their own. So I would sit with them and they would play me the song and then I would write the arrangements while they were sitting there. And what was interesting about it was we worked on the arrangements together. But now I did something that I didn’t realize I did. On the introduction where it started with the concerto [scats] – right after that I wrote the intro to “Stop In The Name of Love.” What was it – and unconsciously I wrote it because it went like this [scats].
